tests.command: Chrome CDP cold full flow and warm coupon reconnect

pagination.before: Unbounded List query loaded and serialized every store row; 100000-row PostgreSQL scans took 20.043 ms for game_plays and 16.690 ms for coupons before decryption and JSON serialization.
pagination.after: Spring Data Page with DB LIMIT/OFFSET, page default 0, size default 50 and max 100; explicit stable page response.

privacy_cleanup.boundary: playedDate < today - 120 days; day 120 retained and day 121 eligible
privacy_cleanup.exception: Linked coupon with status ISSUED and expiresAt >= now is retained until no longer valid.

frontend_bundle.cache_note: Shared chunks were transferred once in the cold flow. Warm coupon reload transferred 0 JS/CSS/font bytes. Rapier has no separate WASM request and is embedded in JS.
frontend_bundle.attribution_boundary: Minified production output did not permit a reliable standalone Drei byte attribution; its bytes are included in the measured game route totals. R3F attribution is a combined R3F/Three chunk.

customer_flow.finding: favicon.ico returned 404 and made the measurement status partial, but the requested customer flow completed.

fifty_store_projection.admin_traffic: At one game-play page plus one coupon page per store per day, measured API JSON is about 0.024 GB/month. Admin page/static traffic is cache-dependent and was not included.

bottlenecks: Rapier embedded chunk is 2.10 MB raw and 0.77 MB gzip.
Pretendard requested 12 subsets and transferred 0.34 MB in the cold flow.
Analytics summary performs eight separate count queries per request.
Game creation takes a store-wide pessimistic write lock, serializing concurrent creates for one store.
Spring Boot measured 434.9 MiB idle in the uncapped container, leaving little headroom at 512 MB.
Store poster PNG is stored as Base64 TEXT in PostgreSQL; growth depends on real poster size and was not reliably measurable from bootstrap data.
cost_risks: Cold customer traffic dominates monthly outbound usage.
Backend 512 MB can approach OOM under load.
Non-PII gameplay/statistics rows are retained after PII anonymization, so database storage continues growing.
Render build and transfer prices are intentionally not hardcoded; apply current pricing to the measured usage.

recommended_render_plan.frontend: Next.js standalone, 512 MB RAM starting point; measured idle 54.88 MiB.
recommended_render_plan.backend: Spring Boot Java 17, 1 GB RAM starting point; do not choose 512 MB without a constrained load test.
recommended_render_plan.postgres: Managed PostgreSQL with at least 5 GB storage and growth alerts; measured table growth is about 0.96 KB per play+coupon pair.
recommended_render_plan.routing: Preserve one public origin and /api routing. If Render cannot provide this across two services, retain a small reverse-proxy service or equivalent platform route.
recommended_render_plan.build_minutes: Observed local Docker steps were 0.78 minutes frontend and 0.53 minutes backend, running in parallel; use actual Render cache behavior for billing.

recommended_followups: Run a constrained 1 GB backend load test and measure peak heap/RSS before launch.
Aggregate the eight analytics counts into one query if admin dashboard latency becomes material.
Evaluate lazy-loading the 3D game stack only after the user enters the game route; current route splitting already prevents it on landing.
Measure real poster PNG sizes before deciding whether PostgreSQL Base64 storage needs object storage.
Add a favicon only if eliminating the harmless 404 matters operationally.
measurement_boundaries: Browser figures are localhost production Docker measurements, not Render edge measurements.
Warm cache means reopening the issued coupon in the same browser profile, not an invalid second play with the same phone.
Pagination HTTP timings are five-request averages on the local machine and include authentication, count query, decryption and JSON serialization.
Cloudflare, LTE/5G and real mobile devices were not measured.
